summary: Backend-only test pass for the Training-Workbook Certificate feature. Created /app/backend/tests/test_certificate_feature.py with 8 focused tests (initial cert shape for psychic + astral modules, quiz-attempt updates certificate + per_lesson_pct, workbook GET includes certificate block, auth guard on certificate endpoint). 8/8 passed on the public preview URL. IMPORTANT: The review-request refers to module id `opening-third-eye`, but the backend does NOT recognise that slug — the real module id is `beginner-1` (its TITLE is 'Opening Your Third Eye'). Frontend (`LessonListModal.tsx:61`) calls `/certificate/${module.id}` which resolves to `beginner-1`, so the feature works end-to-end via the real id. Calling `/certificate/opening-third-eye` returns 200 with `lessons_total=0` and `module_title` echoing the slug — meaning the review-request slug can never earn a certificate. This is either a task-description mismatch or a missing slug alias.

minor.issue: Unknown module_id is silently treated as an empty module (returns 200 with lessons_total=0 and module_title equal to the raw slug). Consider either (a) returning 404 for unknown modules, or (b) mapping slug aliases like `opening-third-eye` → `beginner-1` if that is the intended UX referenced in the review-request.

action_items: Confirm intended module id: review-request says `opening-third-eye`, but backend/frontend use `beginner-1`. If the slug is the desired public id, add an alias (or migrate the id) in TRAINING_MODULES so `/certificate/opening-third-eye` returns lessons_total=5.

Optional hardening: have `GET /api/training-workbook/certificate/{module_id}` return 404 for unknown module ids instead of silently returning a zero-lesson certificate — that would surface the slug mismatch immediately in the UI.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/training_workbook.py::_certificate_status returns lessons_total=0 for unknown modules with the slug echoed as `module_title`. This makes typos/slug mismatches invisible to the client.
routes/training_workbook.py::get_certificate correctly declared BEFORE the `/{module_id}/{lesson_id}` catch-all — good (comment on line 364 makes this explicit).

success_rate.backend: 100% (8/8 passed on the four Certificate-related endpoints)
success_rate.frontend: not tested (per review-request testing_type: backend only)

seed_data_creation: Uses the shared `fresh_user` fixture from conftest.py — a brand-new signup per test session. Quiz attempts written to `training_quiz_attempts` for that throw-away user; no impact on production data or the admin account.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Certificate feature tests live in `/app/backend/tests/test_certificate_feature.py`. They rely on `conftest.py::fresh_user_headers`. The `test_unknown_module_slug_documents_behaviour` test asserts current behaviour (200 + lessons_total=0) for `opening-third-eye`; if main agent adds a slug alias for `opening-third-eye` → `beginner-1`, that test must be updated to expect lessons_total=5 and module_title='Opening Your Third Eye'.
rca_of_issue: The review-request repeatedly names the module `opening-third-eye`, but grep across `/app/backend` and `/app/frontend` shows the id is `beginner-1` in `TRAINING_MODULES` (backend/data/training_content.py:9) and the UI passes that id verbatim to `/api/training-workbook/certificate/${module.id}`. The endpoint accepts any string and short-circuits to `lessons_total=0` when the id is not in TRAINING_MODULES/_ASTRAL_LEVELS, which is why the slug currently 'works' (HTTP 200) but does nothing useful. Fix: either rename the module id or add an alias mapping in `_module_lesson_ids`, `_module_title`, and `_find_lesson`.
